summary: Pastor Jesse Bradley of Grace Community Church in Auburn, Washington, tells Fox News Digital how positive thinking can help when life is hard, drawing on his new book "The Power of the Second Thought." He urges people to reject negative first thoughts and replace them with intentional second thoughts grounded in faith, citing research linking positivity to health and resilience. He also separates real positive thinking from denial or flattery and says Jesus is its greatest source.
one_line: Pastor Jesse Bradley explains how choosing a faith-based "second thought" over negative first thoughts can improve mental health, resilience and outlook.
key_facts: Pastor Jesse Bradley of Auburn, Washington runs Grace Community Church.
Bradley's second book is titled "The Power of the Second Thought," written to help people build habits that strengthen mental health.
Bradley says psychologists report people have between 6,000 and 60,000 thoughts a day.
Bradley says the National Science Foundation shares that up to 80% of our first thoughts are not helpful, even destructive.
Bradley's approach to a positive attitude is "Reject and replace!", e.g. replacing "No one really cares about me" with "God is with me and loves me every day."
Bradley says Johns Hopkins reports that people with a positive outlook are less likely to have a heart attack or cardiovascular event.

Bradley cites University of North Carolina research that positive people are more resilient and find more solutions to problems, and a Harvard study that optimism reduces the risk of dying prematurely.
Bradley graduated from Dartmouth College and was playing professional soccer when he became ill, an illness that took 10 years to fully recover from.
Bradley says he lacked a roadmap for finding hope or tools to handle his loss and pain, and that turning to Jesus and not treating first thoughts as fact was crucial to his mental health.
Bradley says positive thinking is not denial, flattery, self-absorption or creating unrealistic expectations for others, but is realistic, full of truth and love, and aligned with scripture.
Bradley says positive thinking leads to action, rejects excuses, takes responsibility and overcomes setbacks.
Bradley says Jesus brought more positivity than anyone and that "there is no greater source of joy in our lives than God."
